To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the DLIS in cord and maternal blood and in placental extracts are not digoxin, but rather corticosteroids.

(1) DLIS have been extracted from cord serum, placenta and mixed serum (maternal plus cord); (2) DLIS in cord serum and placenta have been partially purified and characterized; (3) a potent inhibitor of the Na+,K+ pump has been identified in a fraction of cord serum which contains progesterone.
the DLIS in cord serum and placental tissue are different substances from those in maternal serum and are not related to digoxin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of immunoreactivity in the cord serum, mixed serum (cord and maternal serum), and placental extracts which cross-react with the antibody for digoxin.
the identification of the immunoreactive substance(s) in cord and maternal sera.
characterising the immunoreactive substances present in cord and maternal sera and placentas which are detected by the digoxin radioimmunoassay.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DLIS in the cord serum is not digoxin, and that the DLIS in cord serum is probably cortisone.
DLIS are present in cord serum in concentrations which are 10- to 1000-fold greater than in maternal serum and in placenta.
the immunoreactive substances are not digoxin and are not identical to digoxin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cortisone and progesterone are the major DLIS in cord serum.
DLIS are present in cord serum in much higher concentration than in normal adult serum and that DLIS are also present in placenta.
DLIS in cord serum and placental tissue is not a specific substance but rather a group of immunoreactive steroids which may have an inhibitory action on the Na+,K+ pump.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DLIS are present in high concentrations in the serum of cord and in placental tissue and that the immunoreactive substance is not digoxin, but is probably related to cortisone and progesterone.
DLIS in cord serum is not digoxin and is not derived from the mother.
the immunoreactive substances in cord and placenta are not identical to digoxin.
